attacks.claim: The new duplicate-ballot log line writes the voter's email alongside the measure and chosen option. Logs ship to a third-party host readable by the whole support team, so a named resident is linked to how they voted, breaking the promise that a ballot is never linkable to identity outside the tally.
attacks.evidence: logger.info("duplicate ballot rejected measure=%s voter=%s choice=%s", measure_id, user.email, body.choice.value)

attacks.claim: Log lines already shipped to the third-party host cannot be recalled from this change. The diff includes no redaction, purge, retention limit, or rollback plan, so the identity-to-choice linkage is effectively irreversible once deployed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no redaction, scrubbing, retention limit, or rollback plan for log lines already shipped to the third-party host

attacks.claim: The results export route has no authentication or role check, unlike the admin-only routes in this module. Anyone who can reach the URL can fetch per-choice counts for any measure id.
attacks.evidence: async def export_results(measure_id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db)): — ABSENT: Depends(require_role("admin"))

attacks.claim: The export does not check whether the measure is closed, although it is described as a tally for closed measures. Calling it on an open measure releases in-progress counts, which leaks interim results and may breach election-release rules.

Counts are keyed by raw Ballot.choice column values but looked up with Choice enum members. If the enum is not str-based or the stored value does not compare equal, every count silently becomes 0 and the council-packet CSV reports zero votes with no error. The PR shows no test of this.
No tests accompany the change. Nothing verifies the auth requirement, the closed-measure gate, zero-count behaviour, or the log content, and the export has not been shown against real data.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no test file or test diff in the PR; the diff touches only app/routes/ballots.py

attacks.claim: The measure slug is interpolated unsanitized into the Content-Disposition header and the CSV cells. Quotes or CR/LF could break the header, and a leading = + - or @ could trigger spreadsheet formula injection when clerks open the file.
Each rejected duplicate attempt emits a log line with no throttle or sampling, so a client repeating the request can flood the third-party log host and inflate ingestion cost.
attacks.evidence: logger.info(...) inside the 409 branch with no throttle

attacks.claim: The change adds only a log line and leaves the 409 message unchanged, so the 'it says I already voted' tickets are not resolved for the user.
attacks.evidence: raise HTTPException(409, "already voted")  (message unchanged; only a log line added)

attacks.claim: The reporting route sits in the ballots module and duplicates the measure lookup and 404 pattern, coupling reporting to voting logic.
